title: ADT + STL
explanation: ADT separates what operations are allowed from how the data is represented. STL gives reusable containers and algorithms so the exam can focus on behavior and tracing.
arabic: الـ ADT يصف العمليات من الخارج بدون تفاصيل الخزن الداخلي. STL يوفر containers و algorithms جاهزة، لذلك أسئلة الفاينل تركز على السلوك والتتبع.
traps: Do not describe ADT by one implementation only.
Know that container choice changes supported operations.
examQuestion: Why is a stack considered an ADT even if it is implemented by an array or linked list?
quickAnswer: Because the required behavior is push/pop/top in LIFO order; the internal representation can change.
deepExplanation: The ADT contract is the public behavior. The implementation can be array-based, linked, or STL-backed as long as the same operations produce the same logical result.

title: Iterators
explanation: An iterator is a pointer-like object for walking through an STL container. begin() points to the first item and end() is the past-the-end sentinel.
arabic: الـ iterator يشبه المؤشر ويمشي داخل الـ container. begin يشير لأول عنصر، و end ليس عنصر بل علامة بعد آخر عنصر.
traps: Do not dereference end().
std::list iterators move with ++/--, not array indexing.
code:
for (auto it = L.begin(); it != L.end(); ++it)
  cout << *it << " ";
examQuestion: Why does the lecture use auto for iterators?
quickAnswer: Iterator type names are long, so auto keeps the traversal readable.
deepExplanation: The compiler knows the exact iterator type from L.begin(). auto preserves type correctness while avoiding complicated type spelling.

title: STL Algorithms
explanation: STL algorithms operate on ranges through iterators. The sorting pages also reinforce the reason sorted data makes searching faster.
arabic: خوارزميات STL تشتغل على ranges بواسطة iterators. صفحات الترتيب توضح أيضاً لماذا البيانات المرتبة تجعل البحث أسرع.
traps: Some algorithms need random-access iterators; std::list does not provide them.
Sorting changes the condition that binary search depends on.
code:
sort(v.begin(), v.end());
auto pos = find(v.begin(), v.end(), target);
examQuestion: Why can binary search eliminate half only after sorting?
quickAnswer: Because the ordering tells us which half cannot contain the target.
deepExplanation: Without sorted order, comparing with the middle element gives no reliable information about the values on either side.

title: Linked List Basics
explanation: A linked list is a chain of nodes. Each node stores data/info plus a link/next pointer to the next node.
arabic: الـ linked list سلسلة عقد. كل عقدة تحتوي data/info ومؤشر link/next للعقدة التالية.
traps: The nodes are not contiguous like an array.
The last node link is NULL in a normal singly linked list.
examQuestion: What two fields must a singly linked-list node contain?
quickAnswer: An information field and a link/next pointer.
deepExplanation: The information field stores the value. The link field stores the address of the next node, which is how traversal proceeds.

title: Linked List Traversal
explanation: Traversal starts from head with a temporary pointer current. Moving current follows links without losing the first node.
arabic: المرور يبدأ من head بواسطة مؤشر مؤقت current. تحريك current يتبع الروابط بدون ضياع أول عقدة.
traps: Moving head during traversal loses the list start.
current->link->info means move one link then read info.
examQuestion: Why should current be used instead of head while traversing?
quickAnswer: head must keep pointing to the first node.
deepExplanation: If head is overwritten, the program may no longer have any pointer to the beginning of the list.

title: Linked List Insert
explanation: Insertion after p must preserve the old next pointer first: newNode->link = p->link; then p->link = newNode.
arabic: الإدخال بعد p لازم يحفظ الرابط القديم أولاً: newNode->link = p->link ثم p->link = newNode.
traps: Reversing the order can make newNode point to itself.
The remainder of the list can become unreachable.
examQuestion: What happens if p->link = newNode is executed before newNode->link = p->link?
quickAnswer: newNode can point back to itself and the rest of the list is lost.
deepExplanation: After p->link changes, p no longer stores the old next node. The second statement copies the wrong address, so the old tail chain is disconnected.

title: Linked List Delete
explanation: Deletion keeps a pointer to the removed node, bypasses it from the previous node, then deallocates it.
arabic: الحذف يحفظ مؤشر للعقدة المحذوفة، ثم يجعل العقدة السابقة تتجاوزها، ثم يحرر الذاكرة.
traps: Do not delete q before reading q->link.
Bypassing removes the node from the chain; it does not shift all nodes.
examQuestion: Why do we assign q = p->link before changing p->link?
quickAnswer: q remembers the node that must be released.
deepExplanation: After bypassing, the previous node points around q. Without q, the deleted node could leak or become impossible to free.

title: Circular Linked List
explanation: A circular linked list changes the last node link so it points back to the first node instead of NULL.
arabic: القائمة الدائرية تجعل رابط آخر عقدة يرجع إلى أول عقدة بدل NULL.
traps: A normal NULL stop condition can become an infinite loop.
Search must stop after returning to the head.
examQuestion: Why does circular display need a count or return-to-head stop rule?
quickAnswer: Because the list does not end with NULL.
deepExplanation: The tail links back to head, so traversal can continue forever unless the algorithm detects one full cycle.

title: std::list
explanation: std::list is an STL abstraction of a doubly linked list. It supports fast insert/erase at known positions through iterators.
arabic: std::list تمثل doubly linked list جاهزة. الإدخال والحذف يكونان سريعَين عند وجود iterator للمكان.
traps: No operator[] random access.
erase invalidates the erased iterator.
examQuestion: Why does std::list not support L[i] like vector?
quickAnswer: Because nodes are linked by pointers and are not stored contiguously.
deepExplanation: To reach an arbitrary node, the list must follow links from a known position. That is why iterator movement is central.

title: Stack
explanation: Stack follows LIFO: the last value pushed is the first value popped. The lecture uses it for history, RPN, binary conversion, and balanced parentheses.
arabic: الـ Stack يعمل LIFO: آخر عنصر يدخل هو أول عنصر يخرج. المحاضرة تستخدمه في history و RPN وتحويل binary وفحص الأقواس.
traps: top() reads without removing.
For RPN, pop val2 first, then val1.
examQuestion: Why does decimal-to-binary use a stack for remainders?
quickAnswer: The remainders are produced in reverse output order.
deepExplanation: The first remainder is the least significant bit. Popping the stack reverses the sequence into the correct binary representation.

title: Queue
explanation: Queue follows FIFO: push enters at the rear and pop removes from the front.
arabic: الـ Queue يعمل FIFO: الإدخال من الخلف rear والحذف من الأمام front.
traps: queue.pop() removes the front, not the back.
front() reads; pop() removes.
examQuestion: Which node becomes front after one pop from A, B, C?
quickAnswer: B becomes the front.
deepExplanation: A entered first, so it is removed first. The next oldest item is B.

title: Deque
explanation: Deque allows insertion and deletion at both front and rear, which makes it natural for palindrome checking.
arabic: الـ Deque يسمح بالإضافة والحذف من البداية والنهاية، لذلك مناسب لفحص palindrome.
traps: Deque is not automatically sorted.
Palindrome logic compares before popping both ends.
examQuestion: Why is deque better than queue for palindrome checking?
quickAnswer: It gives direct access to both front and back.
deepExplanation: A palindrome must compare symmetric endpoints. Queue exposes only the front for removal, while deque exposes both ends.

title: Binary Search
explanation: Binary search works only on sorted data. Every comparison with mid eliminates half of the remaining search range.
arabic: البحث الثنائي يعمل فقط على بيانات مرتبة. كل مقارنة مع mid تستبعد نصف المجال المتبقي.
traps: Unsorted input makes binary search invalid.
Update first/last to mid + 1 or mid - 1, not mid.
examQuestion: Which half is eliminated when target < a[mid]?
quickAnswer: The right half, including mid, is eliminated.
deepExplanation: Because the array is sorted, every value to the right of mid is at least a[mid] and therefore too large.

title: Divide and Conquer
explanation: Divide and conquer splits a problem into smaller similar problems, solves the relevant part, and combines or returns the result.
arabic: تقنية divide and conquer تقسم المشكلة إلى مشاكل أصغر مشابهة، ثم تحل الجزء المناسب وتدمج أو ترجع النتيجة.
traps: The smaller problem must really be smaller.
The base case must stop the splitting.
code:
solve(problem):
  if base_case(problem): return direct_answer
  left, right = divide(problem)
  return conquer(smaller_part)
examQuestion: Why is binary search a divide-and-conquer algorithm?
quickAnswer: It divides the sorted range in half and continues on one smaller half.
deepExplanation: Each step reduces the original search to the same problem on a smaller interval until the target is found or the range is empty.

title: Recursion Basics
explanation: A recursive function calls itself on a smaller input. It must have a base case and must progress toward that base case.
arabic: الدالة recursive تستدعي نفسها على مدخل أصغر. لازم تحتوي base case ولازم تتحرك باتجاهها.
traps: No base case means no stopping.
No progress toward the base case also means no stopping.
examQuestion: Where is the base case in factorial recursion?
quickAnswer: if (n == 0) return 1;
deepExplanation: That case is solved directly and stops new recursive calls. All positive n values reduce toward n == 0.

title: Function Call Stack
explanation: Each function call creates a stack frame with local variables and return information. Recursive calls push frames; completed calls pop frames.
arabic: كل نداء دالة ينشئ stack frame يحتوي المتغيرات ومكان الرجوع. النداءات recursive تضيف frames، وعند الانتهاء يتم pop.
traps: Return values move upward after the base case.
The active frame is always the top frame.
examQuestion: Which frame is active immediately before fact(0) returns?
quickAnswer: The fact(0) frame at the top of the call stack.
deepExplanation: The newest call is on top. When it returns, it is popped and control resumes in the caller frame.

title: Factorial Recursion
explanation: fact(n) waits for fact(n-1). The multiplication is completed while return values propagate upward.
arabic: fact(n) ينتظر fact(n-1). الضرب يكتمل عند رجوع القيم للأعلى.
traps: Do not finish n * fact(n-1) until fact(n-1) returns.
fact(0)=1 is the stopping point.
examQuestion: What is waiting inside fact(3) before fact(2) returns?
quickAnswer: 3 * fact(2).
deepExplanation: fact(3) cannot finish until the recursive call fact(2) produces its return value.

title: Box Traces
explanation: A box trace represents each recursive call as an activation record. Placeholder A stores the value returned by the recursive call.
arabic: الـ box trace يمثل كل نداء recursive كصندوق activation record. الرمز A يمثل قيمة النداء recursive المنتظرة.
traps: Label the recursive call location.
Cross off the completed box only after its return value is substituted in the caller.
code: return n * fact(n - 1); // A
examQuestion: What is substituted into A after fact(0) returns?
quickAnswer: The value 1 is substituted into the caller's A placeholder.
deepExplanation: The base case returns 1. The caller box resumes at point A, fills the placeholder, computes its return value, and then gets crossed off.

title: Recursive power()
explanation: power(x, n) reduces n until n == 0, then multiplies by x while returning back up the stack.
arabic: power(x,n) ينقص n إلى أن يصل n == 0، ثم يضرب في x أثناء الرجوع للأعلى.
traps: The base case for n == 0 returns 1.
Negative n is rejected in the lecture code.
examQuestion: What is the return path for power(2,3)?
deepExplanation: power(2,0) returns 1, then each waiting call multiplies by 2 while the stack unwinds.

title: Binary Search Recursion
explanation: Recursive binary search passes the same array but a smaller first..last range into the next call.
arabic: الـ binary search recursive يمرر نفس المصفوفة لكن بمجال first..last أصغر في كل نداء.
traps: first > last is the not-found base case.
The recursive call must use first..mid-1 or mid+1..last.
examQuestion: What base case returns -1?
quickAnswer: first > last.
deepExplanation: When first passes last, the active search range is empty, so the target is not in the array.

title: Trees and BST
explanation: A BST is a binary tree where left values are smaller and right values are larger. Traversals are recursive and differ only by when the root is processed.
arabic: الـ BST شجرة ثنائية يكون اليسار أصغر واليمين أكبر. الـ traversals هي recursive وتختلف فقط بمكان معالجة الجذر.
traps: Inorder traversal of a BST gives sorted output.
Pre/in/post order depend on root position in the algorithm.
examQuestion: Which traversal prints a BST in sorted order?
quickAnswer: Inorder traversal.
deepExplanation: Inorder visits left subtree, root, then right subtree. In a BST, that means smaller values, then the current value, then larger values.
